title: Circuit model and solder practice
target: Test a circuit representation before making permanent connections.
criteria: Build a complete battery-switch-motor circuit model.
Explain an open versus closed path.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Which connection order describes one complete intended motor circuit?
options: Both motor terminals connected only to the same battery terminal.
Battery positive → switch → motor → unconnected wire.
Battery positive → switch → motor → battery negative.
Battery positive → wire → battery negative, bypassing the motor.
cpa.guide: A closed path includes the source and load, without a bypass short or disconnected return.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A simulation has one broken wire between a switch and motor. The battery is charged. Which change repairs the intended circuit?
options: Remove the motor and expect its axle to turn.
Open a second connection.
Connect the battery terminals directly together.
Reconnect the broken wire to complete the motor path.
cpa.guide: Current through the motor requires a continuous intended circuit, not a short across the battery.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: In a simple battery-switch-motor series model, what changes when the switch is opened?
options: Steady current through the motor stops because the path is broken.
Current doubles because resistance disappears.
The wire turns into an energy source.
The battery loses all stored energy instantly.
cpa.guide: An open switch interrupts the path. Stored battery energy can remain; the model has no steady motor current.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A closed simulated circuit runs its motor. A wire is disconnected while the switch remains closed. Which explanation fits the motor stopping?
options: The motor needs an open path.
The wire used up the current.
Closing the switch destroys charge.
A closed switch alone is insufficient; the whole path must be complete.
cpa.guide: Every part of the series loop must connect. Charge is not consumed by the motor.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Which record supports a supervised solder-practice check without claiming work that did not happen?
options: Record the example joint as your own measurement.
Record the actual inspected scrap joint and the teacher’s feedback after the check.
Write “approved” before soldering.
Use a classmate’s photo as evidence of your joint.
cpa.guide: The record must identify actual work and feedback; a quiz can check this reasoning but not demonstrate soldering skill.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A practice joint needs repair. Which plan follows a safe supervised workflow?
options: Touch the hot tip to check temperature.
Repair it while the circuit is powered.
Disconnect power, let parts cool as needed, and follow the teacher’s soldering procedure.
Skip ventilation and eye protection to save time.
cpa.guide: Work with power disconnected and the required tool safeguards. This question does not certify the student’s physical soldering skill.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.
